title: Company-wide policies and processes — access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, and templates
author: Ava Martinez
summary: Canonical company-wide policies and operational procedures covering access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the set of internal templates. This page centralizes the processes, ownership, approval thresholds, and links to supporting templates and runbooks.
body:
Overview:

This document provides Redwood Inference's canonical, company-wide policies and processes for areas that span multiple teams: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and official internal templates. It defines scope, owners, approval workflows, key thresholds (financial and risk-based), and links to the operational artifacts teams should use.

Intended audience:
- All Redwood employees (policy awareness)
- Team leads and people managers (approvals & delegation)
- Engineers and product managers (access requests, change process)
- Finance, procurement, and legal partners (vendor and purchase processing)
- Security & compliance for high-risk activities

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood corporate and customer-facing systems, cloud accounts, and data stores unless a specific product or customer contract provides a different approved process.
- Exceptions must be documented and approved by Security + People Ops + Finance (see section "Exceptions and escalation").

Owners and roles:
- Policy owner (primary): People Ops (policy custodian)
- Operational owner (day-to-day): Security & Compliance (access & data), Finance (procurement & expenses), IT/Eng Infra (service access & infrastructure changes)
- Approval authorities: Managers, Finance approvers, Legal for contracts, Security for privileged access

1) Access & permissions

Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access to systems and data while enabling teams to move fast.

Principles:
- Least privilege by default; role-based access wherever practical.
- Time-limited elevation for debug/incident work.
- Quarterly access reviews for high-risk scopes.

Process (requesting access):
1. Use the Access Request template (confluence: "access-request-template") and submit via the internal access portal (https://access.redwood.internal).
2. Request must include: justification, scope (resources/paths), requested role, and approver (manager + service owner).
3. Manager approves within 3 business days; Security reviews for privileged roles within 2 business days.
4. Access provisioning is performed by IT/Eng Infra and recorded in the access audit log.

Privileged roles & SSO groups:
- org/admin: requires Security + Head of Engineering approval, 7-day rotating MFA enforcement.
- infra/gpu-pool-ops: requires infra owner approval and on-call acknowledgment.
- data/production-read: requires Data Stewards sign-off (see Data Management section).

Access review cadence:
- High-risk groups (org/admin, billing, production-data): quarterly review.
- Service accounts: monthly automated rotation where supported; manual review quarterly.

Emergency access:
- For incidents, request time-limited elevated access using the Emergency Elevation flow (link to runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/emergency-elevation).
- All emergency elevations must be documented in the incident ticket and reviewed post-incident within 5 business days.

2) Change management

Purpose: Provide safe, observable, and reversible changes to production and critical systems while minimizing approvals for low-risk changes.

Change categories and approval thresholds (table):
| Change type | Examples | Approver(s) | Lead time | Notes |
|-------------|----------|-------------|----------:|-------|
| Standard (low risk) | Configuration tweaks, non-prod deploys | Service owner or team lead | 0-2 business days | No CAB; automated testing required |
| Scheduled (medium risk) | Prod config changes, schema migrations | Service owner + infra lead | 2-5 business days | Requires deployment plan & rollback |
| Major (high risk) | Model serving changes, infra upgrades, DB migrations impacting availability | Engineering Exec + Infra + Security | 5+ business days | CAB review; canary rollout & test plan required |

Change request process:
1. Create a Change Request (CR) using the Change Request template: title = [service] — [brief summary]. Include owner, impact, rollback plan, test plan, schedule, and monitoring dashboard links.
2. Run automated pre-flight checks (CI, integration tests, canary tests).
3. Submit CR to the Change Tracker board; tag reviewers: infra, security, on-call.
4. After approvals, schedule change during agreed maintenance windows unless emergency.
5. Post-change verification checklist executed and recorded.

Emergency changes:
- Allowed only during incident response. Must be retroactively documented in the Change Tracker within 24 hours and reviewed by the CAB at the next meeting.

Change Advisory Board (CAB):
- Membership: Infra lead, Engineering manager, Security engineer, Product representative (rotating), SRE on-call.
- Cadence: Weekly for backlog; ad-hoc for major changes.

3) Data management

Purpose: Protect customer and internal data, ensure correct classification, retention, and secure handling.

Data classification levels:
- Public: information intended for public consumption.
- Internal: routine business data; default classification.
- Restricted: PII, customer data, financials, PHI, or data subject to contract/legal controls.

Requirements:
- All Restricted data must be stored in approved systems with encryption at rest and in transit, access controls, and auditing enabled.
- Data retention: follow the Data Retention Schedule (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/data-retention-schedule).
- Data deletion requests (including customer deletion) handled through the Data Request workflow; Data Stewards coordinate.

Handling rules:
- Never store Restricted data in personal or uncontrolled cloud storage (e.g., personal Google Drive).
- Use redaction or tokenization when possible for logs and debug artifacts.
- Export of Restricted data requires Security and Legal approval.

Quarterly checks and audits:
- Data Stewards run a quarterly inventory of Restricted datasets and verify access lists.
- Audit results and remediation plans are tracked in the Data Inventory board.

4) Procurement & expenses

Purpose: Govern how Redwood purchases services, hardware, and reimburses employees while preserving budget controls and compliance.

Approval thresholds:
- <= $1,000: Team lead approval (expense reimbursement or purchase card).
- $1,001 — $25,000: Finance approval + manager.
- > $25,000: Finance + Legal + Executive sponsor (Director or above).

Procurement steps (standard vendor):
1. Complete the Purchase Request form (template: /confluence/policies-and-process/procurement-request-template). Include business justification, budget code, and desired vendor terms.
2. Finance evaluates budget availability and issues PO for approved purchases.
3. For contracts > $25k, route to Legal for review and to Security if the purchase involves access to customer data or infrastructure.
4. IT/Infra will provision equipment or accounts upon receipt and confirmation of delivery/credentials.

Expense reimbursement:
- Submit using the Expenses app with receipts attached, within 30 days of expenditure.
- Manager approval required; late submissions require manager + Finance approval.

Travel policy (brief):
- Book travel through approved vendor/portal (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/travel-booking).
- Per-diem and allowable expenses defined in the Travel Expense template.
- All international travel that involves customer visits or access to restricted datasets requires pre-approval from Security + Travel coordinator.

5) Vendor management

Purpose: Ensure we engage vendors consistently, assess risk, and maintain contract visibility.

Vendor lifecycle steps:
1. Intake: submit Vendor Intake form (template). Provide service description, data access needs, and estimated spend.
2. Risk assessment: Security performs a standard vendor risk review (questions on data handling, encryption, SOC/ISO certifications).
3. Contracting: Legal reviews terms; Finance confirms payment terms and GL coding.
4. Onboarding: Assign vendor owner, create access controls, add vendor to Vendor Registry.
5. Ongoing: Quarterly health checks for critical vendors; annual reviews for risk posture.

Escalation: If a vendor fails security or performance requirements, the vendor owner must open an escalation ticket with Legal + Security and pause new purchases.

6) Travel policy (expanded)

General rules:
- Employees should choose reasonable economy travel unless approved by Director-level or above.
- Use corporate travel portal for bookings; exceptions require manager sign-off.
- Foreign travel with customer meetings: Security must review device protection and data handling plans.

Travel approvals and per-diem:
1. Create a Travel Authorization request with itinerary and purpose.
2. Manager approves; Finance reviews for high-value trips (> $5,000).
3. Use approved expense template for reimbursements.

Emergency travel changes:
- Use the travel booking vendor's change support and notify People Ops for rebooking assistance.

7) Internal templates and artifacts

The following templates are maintained in this space and should be used for all formal requests: 
- access-request-template (Access requests)
- change-request-template (Change management)
- procurement-request-template (Purchases & PO)
- vendor-intake-template (Vendor onboarding)
- travel-authorization-template (Travel approvals)
- expense-reimbursement-template (Expenses)
- incident-elevation-template (Emergency access / incident changes)

Using templates ensures consistent approvals, auditing, and faster processing. Always attach the template output to tickets and archive final documents in the related project page.

Exception handling and escalation:
- To request an exception to any policy, submit the Policy Exception form with justification, risk mitigation, and time-limited plan.
- Exceptions require People Ops + Security + Finance sign-off.
- Policy exceptions are tracked centrally and reviewed quarterly.

Training and rollout:
- New hires receive a policy overview during onboarding.
- Team leads must run a 30-minute policy refresh each quarter with their teams.
- People Ops will run annual training on data handling and access controls.

Audit, metrics, and enforcement:
- Key metrics tracked monthly: number of access requests, time-to-approve, number of exceptions, procurement cycle time, overdue expense reports.
- Security will run quarterly audits of privileged access and produce remediation work items.
- Violations are handled per the company disciplinary policy (see company handbook).

B. Example Change Request (abbreviated):
Title: model-serving-2026-06 — upgrade transformer runtime
Owner: Model Serving Team
Impact: 10% reduction in latency; risk of brief 5-10m rollout pause
Rollback: revert to previous image and drain traffic to canary
Test plan: automated integration + canary for 1h at 1% traffic
Schedule: 2026-07-05 02:00-04:00 UTC
Approvals: infra lead (signed), security (signed)
